faq.title: Prices and penalties, in short.
faq.subtitle: What each key covers, which Windows switches stay on, and what a penalty can still do.

items.q: What are the three prices, and are the keys shared?
items.a: Rust Cheats and UGC Account recovery are $35 for 30 days or $150 lifetime. HWID Spoofer is $50 for 30 days or $150 lifetime. The products page lists them as three checkouts, not one bundle.

items.q: Does a lifetime menu key also cover the hardware tool?
items.a: No. Lifetime on Rust Cheats covers that product only. The HWID spoofer and UGC recovery are separate keys. The spoofer is $50 monthly or $150 lifetime. The menu and UGC are $35 monthly or $150 lifetime. Paying for a month does not create a credit toward lifetime.

items.q: Can support move the menu key onto another computer for free?
items.a: Write support with the order email. If new accounts fail on that machine, the next purchase is the HWID Spoofer. That is not a free transfer of the menu key.

items.q: Which operating systems and Windows switches are required?
items.a: Windows 10 or 11 on Intel or AMD. HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot stay on. macOS and Linux are not supported.

items.q: What shows up in the portal after payment?
items.a: The portal for the product you paid for, with that product’s loader. Tune the menu, then store a config. Leave HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot on.

items.q: What do the green, red, and blue status labels mean?
items.a: Green means the build is updated and can be used. Red means it is not updated and should stay closed. Blue means developers are still updating it.

items.q: Can EasyAnti-Cheat still act on the account?
items.a: Yes. EasyAnti-Cheat can penalize the account. Nothing on this site promises that a session will avoid a penalty.

items.q: New accounts fail on this PC and work on another. Is that the menu key?
items.a: That pattern is a hardware flag on the PC. The matching product is the HWID Spoofer, sold on its own. It does not lift an account-only restriction, and lifetime on Rust Cheats does not include it.

items.q: What does the appeal workspace actually change?
items.a: UGC Account recovery holds templates, evidence lists, and follow-up reminders. It does not promise the account comes back, and it is not the HWID spoofer.

items.q: Which product matches a PC that rejects new accounts?
items.a: Buy HWID Spoofer when a new account fails on one PC and works on another. That purchase does not clear an account-only restriction. Use UGC Account recovery for the account case.

items.q: Does this checkout include a DMA card?
items.a: No. Rust Cheats is a Windows loader from the portal. A DMA device is a different product and is not what this key delivers. Do not run a file you found in a search result.

items.q: Do camera FOV and aim FOV share one slider?
items.a: No. Camera FOV sets how wide the view is. Aim FOV is only the cone the assist searches. Set the camera first, then adjust aim FOV again.

items.q: Does visible check stop boxes from drawing through cover?
items.a: No. Visible check only decides when aim assist may engage: in line of sight, not through solid cover. Skeleton and box ESP are separate toggles and can still draw while that check is on.

items.q: Aim keeps sticking to a downed player. Which toggle changes that?
items.a: Turn on Ignore Knocked so aim assist skips players who are already down. Show Knocked only keeps those bodies on the overlay. Turning one on does not turn the other off.

items.q: The aim filter is already on. What does bone selection still do?
items.a: The filter limits which models the assist may pick. Bone selection then prefers Closest, Head, Neck, or Chest on those models. Set the filter first, then the bone.

items.q: Can one of the aim keys be a controller button without a remap app?
items.a: Yes. This build has two aim keys, and one of them can be a native controller bind. You do not install a separate remap app for that second key.

items.q: Player labels cover the fight. What should stay on first?
items.a: Leave box or skeleton, health, and distance. Add gear levels only if you actually read them. A max distance drops far players. Weapon options are another menu, not a substitute for those labels.

items.q: How do I separate groups without adding more boxes?
items.a: Use team number, hero name, and view direction. A head circle marks the head hitbox. Snaplines run from your view to a player. Leave helmet, armor, and chest-bag levels off until you read them.

items.q: Item names still fill every container. What do I change first?
items.a: Set a minimum price so cheaper items drop off. Keep player corpses, AI corpses, and computers as their own markers instead of hiding the whole loot group. Color, size, transparency, and brightness sit on the player visual group, not on that price floor.

items.q: Are smooth, stickiness, and speed the same slider?
items.a: No. Smooth slows how fast the crosshair closes the gap. Stickiness holds the assist on the current player a little longer when they strafe or leave the edge of the cone. Speed is a third slider: how fast the assist moves once a target is already inside that cone. Change one, then save the config.

items.q: Do arm scale and weapon scale move the same mesh?
items.a: No. Arms scale offset moves the arms on X, Y, and Z. Weapon scale offset moves the gun on its own axes. Enable Crosshair only draws a fixed center mark. Third person is a separate hotkey and does not change either scale.

items.q: Does combat mode switch aim off?
items.a: No. Combat mode hides the markers you pick: player, AI, item, dead container, or computer. Aim and misc options stay on until you toggle those groups yourself.

items.q: What is the encryption bypass line under Misc?
items.a: It is one Misc menu option in this build. It is not a second product and it is not a hardware card. Leave it off unless the current note on cheatsforrust.net says to use it for this client.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: cheatsforrust.net sells three Windows products: Rust Cheats, a hardware tool, and an appeal workspace. The menu is one product: aim, visuals, weapon options, misc options, and config options. It is not a Lite, Pro, and Elite ladder, and it is not a DMA card.

The menu and the appeal workspace are $35 for 30 days or $150 lifetime. The hardware tool is $50 for 30 days or $150 lifetime. Lifetime on the menu does not include the other two. A month does not create a credit toward lifetime.

Product names on this site identify what we sell. They are not a claim that the game publisher endorses the software. Delivery is a portal download for Windows 10 or 11. You keep HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot on, then open the loader only when the site still matches the current client.

sections.heading: What we publish
paragraphs: The [Rust Cheats](/product/rust-cheat/) page lists the menu names and the Windows requirements: Windows 10 or 11, Intel or AMD, with HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot left on. The [products page](/products/) is where you compare the cheat, the [HWID Spoofer](/product/spoofer/), and [UGC Account recovery](/product/ugc/).

Guides on the [blog](/blog/) explain aim FOV versus camera FOV, how loot filters work, and why a hardware flag is a different buy from an account appeal. The [forum](/forum/) is for those same questions, with developer replies marked on the thread. Read the [terms](/terms/) before checkout. Sales are final, including bans.

EasyAnti-Cheat can still act on an account. Nothing here is a guarantee that a session stays clean after the next patch. Check this site after a client update before you open the loader. If the page is not current for that build, leave the software closed. Open the [status page](/status/) before every launch. Green means the published build can be used. Red means leave the loader closed. Blue means the build is still being updated.

Status notes on the homepage describe whether the published build still matches the client. They are not a promise that EasyAnti-Cheat will ignore the software. If you are unsure, leave the loader closed and read the matching guide on the blog before you queue again.

sections.heading: Support
paragraphs: Loader errors, a key that will not move, and checkout questions go through the [support page](/support/). Include the order email, Windows version, and the exact loader text. Do not turn HVCI, core isolation, TPM, or secure boot off because a chat message from another game said to.

sections.heading: Refunds and purchases
paragraphs: All sales are final once checkout completes. We do not refund change-of-mind purchases, account bans, EasyAnti-Cheat penalties, or issues caused by ignoring the setup notes or launching while the site is not current for that patch.

If the product does not work as described on a supported setup—Windows 10 or 11 with HVCI, core isolation, TPM, and secure boot on, and the current loader from the portal—contact us through the Support page. Include your order email, Windows version, and the exact loader text.
We may, at our discretion, offer a fix, replacement access, or partial/full refund when we confirm a fault on our side. We are not obligated to approve every request.

paragraphs: Third-party tools for Rust can conflict with game updates and EasyAnti-Cheat. You use this software at your own risk, including possible account action.
Check the homepage status banner before every session. Do not queue ranked while modules are offline or misaligned after a patch.
